reagents.name: NaBH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild hydride source. Reduces aldehydes and ketones to alcohols. Does NOT reduce esters, amides, or carboxylic acids.

reagents.name: LiAlH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong hydride reducer: reduces aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acids, amides, nitriles, epoxides.
reagents.conditions: Anhydrous Et2O or THF; acidic workup

reagents.name: DIBAL-H
reagents.whatItDoes: Selective 1-equivalent reducer. At -78 C with 1 eq, stops ester reduction at the aldehyde.

reagents.name: PCC
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild oxidant. 1° alcohols → aldehydes (stops there). 2° alcohols → ketones.

reagents.name: DMP
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild, selective oxidant. 1° alcohols → aldehydes; 2° alcohols → ketones. More selective than PCC, tolerates sensitive FGs.

reagents.name: Swern oxidation
reagents.whatItDoes: Metal-free oxidation of 1° alcohols to aldehydes, 2° to ketones. No Cr contamination.

reagents.name: Jones (CrO3/H2SO4)
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong oxidant. 1° alcohols → carboxylic acids. 2° alcohols → ketones.

reagents.name: Na2Cr2O7/H2SO4
reagents.whatItDoes: Classic chromium(VI) oxidant. 1° to COOH (aqueous), 2° to ketones. Also oxidizes phenol to benzoquinone.

reagents.name: NaH
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong, non-nucleophilic base. Deprotonates alcohols, amides, NH, acidic C-H. Releases H2 gas.
reagents.example: R-OH + NaH → R-O- Na+ + H2 (for Williamson)

reagents.name: TMSCl / Et3N
reagents.whatItDoes: Protects an OH as a silyl ether (R-OTMS). Base scavenges HCl.

reagents.name: TBAF
reagents.whatItDoes: Cleaves silyl ethers (TMS, TBS, TBDPS) back to the free alcohol via strong Si-F affinity.

reagents.name: PBr3
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts 1° and 2° alcohols to alkyl bromides with inversion. Milder than HBr.

reagents.name: SOCl2 / pyridine
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts alcohols to alkyl chlorides (inversion). Converts COOH to acyl chlorides.
reagents.conditions: Neat or CH2Cl2; pyridine to scavenge HCl

reagents.name: TsCl / pyridine
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts R-OH to R-OTs. OTs is an excellent LG, enabling SN2 or E2 that OH can't do directly.
reagents.conditions: CH2Cl2 or pyridine, 0 C to room temperature

reagents.name: Hg(OAc)2, H2O; then NaBH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Markovnikov hydration of an alkene via mercurinium bridge. NO carbocation rearrangements.

reagents.name: Hg(OAc)2, ROH; then NaBH4
reagents.whatItDoes: Markovnikov ether synthesis from alkene + alcohol. No rearrangement. Works for 3° ethers.

reagents.name: HBr / peroxide (ROOR, hv)
reagents.whatItDoes: Anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr to alkene via radical chain. Only HBr works.
reagents.conditions: ROOR or hv initiator; CCl4 or neat

reagents.name: NBS
reagents.whatItDoes: Low-concentration Br2 for allylic/benzylic radical bromination. Does NOT add across alkenes.

reagents.name: mCPBA
reagents.whatItDoes: Epoxidation of alkenes (syn, stereospecific). Also Baeyer-Villiger (ketone → ester) and S oxidations.

reagents.name: Ti(OiPr)4, tBuOOH, DET
reagents.whatItDoes: Enantioselective epoxidation of allylic alcohols. (+)-DET and (-)-DET give opposite enantiomers.

reagents.name: NaIO4
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild oxidant. Sulfides → sulfoxides (stops there). Also cleaves vicinal diols.

reagents.name: H2O2 (excess)
reagents.whatItDoes: Oxidizes sulfides and sulfoxides all the way to sulfones.

reagents.name: NaSH
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts alkyl halides to thiols via SN2 (soft, strong nucleophile).

reagents.name: Br2 / NaOH / H2O
reagents.whatItDoes: Oxidizes two thiols to a disulfide (R-S-S-R). Biologically relevant chemistry.

reagents.name: Zn / HCl
reagents.whatItDoes: Reduces disulfides back to thiols. Also reduces aromatic nitro groups to amines.

reagents.name: Sn / HCl (or Fe/HCl, H2/Pd)
reagents.fullName: Tin or iron in acid; H2/Pd
reagents.whatItDoes: Reduces aromatic nitro groups to primary amines.

reagents.name: CuCl / CuBr / CuCN (Sandmeyer)
reagents.whatItDoes: Replace ArN2+ with Cl, Br, CN. Also H3PO2 → H, HBF4/heat → F, H2O/heat → OH.
reagents.conditions: ArN2+ first made from ArNH2 + NaNO2/HCl at 0 C

reagents.name: H2 / Lindlar
reagents.fullName: Pd/CaCO3 poisoned with Pb and quinoline
reagents.whatItDoes: Alkyne → Z-alkene (cis). Stops at alkene; no over-reduction.

reagents.name: Na / NH3(l)
reagents.whatItDoes: Alkyne → E-alkene (trans). Also Birch reduction of aromatics.
reagents.conditions: Liquid NH3, Na metal; EtOH co-solvent for Birch

reagents.name: BH3·THF; then H2O2/NaOH
reagents.whatItDoes: Anti-Markovnikov hydration of alkenes. Syn addition. No rearrangement.

reagents.name: O3; then DMS
reagents.whatItDoes: Cleaves C=C into two C=O groups. DMS workup gives aldehydes/ketones; H2O2 workup gives COOH.
reagents.conditions: CH2Cl2, -78 C; then DMS or H2O2

reagents.name: KMnO4, hot
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong oxidant. Cleaves alkenes to COOH/ketone. Oxidizes benzylic C-H to COOH.

reagents.name: Ph3P=CR2 (Wittig)
reagents.whatItDoes: Converts aldehydes/ketones to alkenes via oxaphosphetane; byproduct Ph3P=O.
reagents.conditions: THF, room temperature. Ylide from Ph3P + alkyl halide + n-BuLi.

reagents.name: LDA
reagents.whatItDoes: Strong, bulky, non-nucleophilic base. Generates the KINETIC enolate at -78 C.

reagents.name: NaOMe / NaOEt (equilibrating)
reagents.whatItDoes: Equilibrating base — forms the THERMODYNAMIC enolate (more substituted).

reagents.name: H3O+ (dilute)
reagents.whatItDoes: Protonates alkoxides/carbanions after nucleophilic addition; hydrolyzes imines, acetals, enol ethers.

reagents.name: NaCN (SN2 then hydrolyze)
reagents.whatItDoes: SN2 on 1° alkyl halide → R-CN (one-C extension). Hydrolyze to R-COOH.

reagents.name: NaBH3CN
reagents.whatItDoes: Mild hydride for reductive amination. Selectively reduces iminium over C=O at mildly acidic pH.

reagents.name: NaOH (saponification)
reagents.whatItDoes: Hydrolyzes esters to carboxylate + alcohol (irreversible, driven by deprotonation).

reagents.name: Br2 / FeBr3 (EAS)
reagents.whatItDoes: Electrophilic aromatic bromination of benzene and activated arenes.

reagents.name: HNO3 / H2SO4 (nitration)
reagents.whatItDoes: Electrophilic aromatic nitration (generates NO2+).
reagents.conditions: Mix at 0 C; add to arene

reagents.name: AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts)
reagents.whatItDoes: Lewis acid for FC acylation (RCOCl) and alkylation (RCl). Fails on strongly deactivated arenes.

reagents.name: NaNH2
reagents.whatItDoes: Very strong base. Deprotonates terminal alkynes; drives benzyne; Hofmann E2.

reagents.name: Ac2O (acetic anhydride)
reagents.whatItDoes: Acetylates alcohols (-OAc) and amines (-NHAc). Common NH2 protection on aromatic amines before EAS.

reagents.name: Weinreb amide + RMgX
reagents.whatItDoes: Lets you stop Grignard addition at the KETONE (not tertiary alcohol). Metal chelation stabilizes the intermediate.
